text:
MPC fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as oil prices weakened and refinery margins compressed. US crude dropped to $82.24 per barrel while refineries ran at 97.5% capacity with elevated fuel inventories—gasoline storage at 217.7 million barrels and diesel at 105.6 million barrels. When refineries are running flat-out but storage is building, the profit margin refiners earn on each barrel shrinks, which directly cuts into Marathon's earnings.

The broader headwind is a shift in market sentiment around energy. Climate talks collapsed over the weekend without committing to phase out fossil fuels, which might have spooked investors expecting tighter long-term supply—instead, the lack of a binding agreement suggests oil demand concerns remain. At the same time, the news cycle is focusing on alternative energy solutions (quantum computing for grid optimization, hydrogen) and geopolitical oil reallocation (Lukoil assets), not on refining strength, which may have pushed money out of refiners like MPC into other sectors.
